title: Prompt Like a Pro: 10 LLM Tricks That Actually Work
subtitle: Clear, practical prompting moves that get better answers with less back-and-forth.

intro.title: Why Prompts Matter
paragraphs: A model can only work with what you give it. Better instructions usually mean better output.
Use these tricks as templates and adjust the wording for your project, audience, and output format.

items.title: 1) Define the role
items.body: Tell the model who it is and what skillset to use.

code.content: You are a senior editor. Rewrite this for clarity and tone for high school readers.

items.title: 2) Add context
items.body: Include audience, goal, and constraints in plain language.

code.content:
Audience: non-technical managers
Goal: one-page summary
Constraints: avoid jargon, keep it under 180 words

items.title: 3) Specify output format
items.body: Ask for the shape you want, not just the content.

code.content: Return: title, 5 bullet points, and a 2-line conclusion.

items.title: 4) Ask for options
items.body: Get multiple variations and choose the best one.

code.content: Give me 3 versions: concise, friendly, and formal.

items.title: 5) Ask for a self-check
items.body: Have the model verify if it followed your rules.

code.content: Before finalizing, confirm you met every constraint in a checklist.

callout.text: This catches missing pieces before you paste the output somewhere else.

items.title: Be specific about what is wrong
items.body: Replace vague feedback like "better" with exact edits.

code.content: Too long. Cut 35%. Keep examples 1 and 3. Remove buzzwords.

items.title: Use iterative prompts
items.body: Ask for one improvement at a time: structure, then tone, then detail.

code.content:
Step 1: improve structure only.
Step 2: make tone more conversational.
Step 3: add one concrete example.

items.title: Too broad
items.body: If your request is vague, the answer will be vague.

items.title: No audience
items.body: Always say who the output is for.

items.title: No format
items.body: Ask for headings, bullets, tables, or JSON when needed.

items.title: One-shot only
items.body: Refine in rounds instead of expecting perfect output once.

footer.heading: Prompting Is a Skill
footer.text: Good prompts are less about magic words and more about clear instructions.
